The procedure is written to notes/procedure.md, and all three notes files now pass check_file with zero banned words and zero long sentences.

## Background

The task was to write a reusable fix procedure, then apply it to notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md.

## Relevance

All sandbox notes now comply with the style rules, so agents can follow the same steps on future files.

## Information

The check_file tool confirmed the fixes: a.md had one banned word ("clearly"), now removed [1]. b.md had one sentence over 25 words, now split into three sentences [1]. c.md had one banned word ("very") and one long sentence, both fixed [1]. Meaning was kept in each file.

## End

arguments.content:
# Procedure: fix banned words and long sentences in one notes file

1. Run check_file on the file. Note each banned word and each sentence over 25 words.
2. Read the file to see the full text.
3. Rewrite each flagged sentence:
   a. Remove the banned word, or replace it with a factual term or a number.
   b. Split any sentence over 25 words into two or more sentences under the limit.
4. Keep the meaning of the file. Do not add or remove facts.
5. Write the fixed text to the file with write_file.
6. Run check_file again on the file.
7. Confirm zero banned words and zero sentences over 25 words. If not, go back to Step 3.

# Release note

The new parser is faster than the old one. It reads a large log in two seconds.

# Incident note

The outage started when the cache filled up during the nightly import. The service fell back to the database for every request. This lasted until the import job ended an hour later.

# Design note

The queue is simple. Each worker takes one message and runs the job. The worker writes the result to the store and marks the message as done, so no other worker picks it up again.
